chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the life, family relationships, reign, exile, and military activities of Diarmait Ua Briain, an 11th-century Irish king.
chunks.page_content: Diarmait Ua Briain was involved in a four-year struggle for control of Munster after banishing Muirchertach Ua Briain. Diarmait Ua Briain succeeded Muirchertach Ua Briain as acting King of Munster in 1114. Diarmait Ua Briain was one of three sons of Toirdelbach Ua Briain. Muirchertach Ua Briain eventually captured Diarmait Ua Briain. Diarmait Ua Briain attacked Muirchertach Ua Briain and Brian Ua Briain in 1116. Muirchertach Ua Briain made peace with Diarmait Ua Briain after the siege of Limerick. Diarmait Ua Briain was an 11th-century Irish king. Diarmait Ua Briain lived in exile for several years. Conchobar Ua Briain of Thomond was a son of Diarmait Ua Briain. Diarmait Ua Briain ruled Munster from 1114 to 1118. Muirchertach Ua Briain ruled as King of Munster while Diarmait Ua Briain lived in exile. Diarmait Ua Briain died in Cork in 1118. Diarmait Ua Briain violated a mutual oath on the relics of Ireland when attacking Muirchertach Ua Briain and Brian Ua Briain in 1116. Diarmait Ua Briain besieged Limerick in 1116. Diarmait Ua Briain is believed to have been the commander of the Irish fleet that supported Rhys ap Tewdwr at the Battle of Mynydd Carn. Muirchertach Ua Briain banished Diarmait Ua Briain from Munster shortly after the death of their father in 1086. Diarmait Ua Briain recognized Muirchertach Ua Briain's claim in 1093. Diarmait Ua Briain was installed as "dux" of Waterford in 1093. Diarmait Ua Briain reconciled with Muirchertach Ua Briain in 1093.
